home.h1: Describe it. Don't say it. Score.
home.lead: Bombardiro is a party word game for football fans. One player describes, the team guesses, and every word they get before the whistle is a goal.

steps.title: Describe, don't say
steps.text: A card shows 5 to 8 football words. Describe each one without saying it.

steps.title: Every guess is a goal
steps.text: Tap each word your team gets. Clear the card and a fresh one drops on the same clock.

steps.title: The whistle ends it
steps.text: Only the timer ends a turn. Pass the phone to the next team.

words.title: Every word is football
words.text: Players, clubs, stadiums, legends, tactics and trophies, World Cup moments: nearly 1,700 words in every language. Easy deals the household names. Hard deals the deep cuts.

room.title: One phone. 2–4 teams.
room.text: Name your teams, pick a crest and pass the phone around the room. No account, no sign-up, no second device.

fair.title: No arguments
fair.text: Once a team reaches the target, the round is played out so everyone gets the same number of turns. Level at the top? Extra round. Someone shouted the answer as the whistle blew? Open the last turn, switch the word between GOAL and MISS, and the score fixes itself.

anywhere.title: Plays anywhere
anywhere.text: Every word is already inside the app, so it works on a plane, in a basement or with no signal at all. New and corrected words arrive on their own, with no app update needed.

languages.title: Speaks your language
languages.text: Play in English, Russian or Armenian. The words are translated by people, not machines.

final.title: Crown the champions
final.text: Grab your friends, pick your categories and start the match.

meta.title: How to play Bombardiro: football Alias rules
meta.description: The rules in a minute: pick categories, line up 2–4 teams, describe the words without saying them and beat the whistle. Settings and fair-play rules explained.

howToPlay.lead: Describe the word. Don't say it. Score the goal.

steps.title: Pick your categories
steps.text: Choose the categories you want in the match: players, clubs, World Cup and more.

steps.title: Line up teams
steps.text: Add 2–4 teams, name them and pick a crest. Then pass the phone around the table.

steps.title: Describe, don't say it
steps.text: The active player describes the words on the card. Saying the word itself is a foul: leave it unmarked and move on to the next.

steps.title: Tap a word, score a goal
steps.text: When your team guesses it, tap the word to bank a goal. Tap again to undo a mistake.

steps.title: Beat the clock
steps.text: Score as many as you can before the whistle. The clock ends the turn, or tap END to finish it early.

steps.title: First to the target wins
steps.text: Hand off and repeat. Once a team reaches the target, the round is played out so everyone gets equal turns, and the top score lifts the trophy.

items.label: Turn time
items.text: How many seconds one player gets to describe words. When the time runs out, the turn passes to the next team.

items.label: Words per card
items.text: How many words are dealt on one card. Clear them all and a fresh card arrives on the same clock: the timer ends the turn, not the card.

items.label: Points to win
items.text: The target score for the match. Once a team reaches it, the round is played out so every team gets the same number of turns, then the highest score wins. A tie at the top plays another round.

items.label: Number of teams
items.text: How many teams the match starts with. You can rename them, pick crests, and add or remove teams before kick-off.

items.label: Difficulty
items.text: Which word pool the cards come from. Easy uses the best-known words in your categories, Hard the more obscure ones.

fair.title: Fair to the last kick
items: No word repeats in a match until your chosen categories run out.
Once a team reaches the target, the round is played out so everyone gets the same number of turns.
Level at the top? An extra round decides it.
Missed a tap as the whistle blew? Tap the latest score on the scoreboard and switch the word between GOAL and MISS.

tips.title: How to describe well
items: Players: try the club, the position, the country or a famous moment.
Clubs: try the city, the nickname, the colours or the biggest rival.
Stadiums: try the city, the home team or a match everyone remembers.
Stuck? Leave the word unmarked and move on. The clock won't wait.

meta.title: Bombardiro support: help and questions
meta.description: Answers about accounts, offline play, languages and your data, plus how to reach us if something in Bombardiro isn't working.

support.lead: If something is broken, confusing or missing, write to us.

contact.title: Write to us
contact.inApp: You can also reach the same inbox from inside the app: Settings › Report a bug. That opens a mail composer with the app version and your iOS version already filled in, which makes problems much faster to track down.
contact.response: We read everything. Replies usually take a couple of days.

items.a: No. There is no sign-up, no login and no profile. The game never asks who you are.

Yes. Every word ships inside the app, so you can play on a plane, in a basement or with the connection off. The app checks for new words when it has a connection and uses them the next time you launch, so a download never interrupts a game in progress.

English, Russian and Armenian. The app follows your device language on first launch. After that you can change it any time from the language menu at the top left of the home screen. Words are translated, not machine-generated.

items.q: Can I add my own words?
items.a: No. The six categories are fixed, and new or corrected words arrive on their own. If a turn was scored wrong, tap the latest score on the scoreboard to switch any of its words between GOAL and MISS.

items.q: The app is showing the wrong language or theme.
items.a: Both are remembered on your device once you change them, so they stop following your system setting. Set them from the home screen: the language menu is at the top left, the theme button at the top right.

items.q: I found a word that is wrong, offensive or misspelled.
items.a: Please tell us, and include the word and the language. Words are updated over the air, so a fix reaches everyone without an app update.

items.q: How do I delete my data?
items.a: There is no account to delete. Scores and team names are never saved. Your settings are saved only on your device, so uninstalling the app removes them, although a device backup may still hold a copy. The app collects no statistics about how you play. The crash reports it sends are filed under random identifiers, not your name or email, and are deleted on a fixed schedule. Because they aren't tied to your name or email, an email from you usually doesn't let us find them, but write to us anyway and we'll explain what we can do. See the app's privacy policy for the full detail.

items.q: How do I turn off game reminders?
items.a: In the app, open Settings › Game reminders. It takes you to Bombardiro's page in the iOS Settings app, where you can switch notifications off or back on. The row appears once the app has asked you about notifications, after your first finished match.

items.q: Does it cost anything? Are there ads?
items.a: The game is free. It has no purchases and shows no ads.

meta.title: Website privacy notice | Bombardiro
meta.description: What bombardiro.app collects and what it doesn't: no sign-up, no ads and no tracking across other websites.

privacy.intro: This notice covers the website bombardiro.app. The Bombardiro app has its own privacy policy.

sections.title: Who runs this site
sections.text: Bombardiro is published by Gor Ghazaryan, Armenia. You can reach us at bombardiro.dev@gmail.com.

sections.title: The short version
sections.text: We don't ask for your name or email. This site shows no ads, sets no cookies of its own and doesn't track you across other websites.

sections.title: Visit statistics
sections.text: We use Vercel Web Analytics to count visits and Vercel Speed Insights to measure how fast pages load. Neither uses third-party cookies. Web Analytics tells visits apart with a temporary value made from the incoming request, which is discarded after 24 hours. We see totals such as the page, the referring site, the country, the browser, the operating system and the device type, not individual people.

sections.title: Hosting
sections.text: Vercel hosts this site. Like any web host, it receives technical details of each request, such as your IP address, so it can deliver pages and keep the service secure. Vercel handles this under its own privacy notice.

sections.title: Links to other services
sections.text: Buttons for the App Store, Instagram and TikTok take you to those services. Once you're there, their own privacy policies apply.

sections.title: Emails
sections.text: If you write to us, we receive your email address and your message, and use them only to reply. Our mailbox is a Gmail account, so Google stores these emails for us.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You can ask us what we hold about you, and ask us to correct or delete it, by writing to bombardiro.dev@gmail.com.

sections.title: Changes
sections.text: If this notice changes, we'll update this page and the date above.
